**EB-2 NIW 的 Dhanasar 三项标准**（*Matter of Dhanasar*, 26 I&N Dec. 884, AAO 2016 年 12 月 27 日）

申请人须同时满足以下三点，才能获得国家利益豁免（NIW），免除工作证明和劳工证（PERM）要求：

1. **拟议工作具有实质性价值和国家重要性（substantial merit and national importance）**：工作领域要有实际价值，且影响范围超出单一雇主或地方，例如对某一领域、地区或全国产生广泛影响。
2. **申请人有能力推进该工作（well positioned to advance the proposed endeavor）**：看申请人的教育背景、专业经验、过往成就、具体计划，以及是否已有实际推进或他人认可。
3. **综合权衡，豁免劳工证对美国更有利（on balance, beneficial to the U.S. to waive the job offer and labor certification）**：比较走正常 PERM 流程与豁免之间的利弊，例如紧迫性、劳工证程序是否不切实际等。

申请人还须先符合 EB-2 基本资格，才会进入上述三项评估。

**来源：**
- [Matter of Dhanasar 相关概述（Wikipedia, National Interest Waiver）](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Interest_Waiver)
- [NatLawReview：第一项标准深入分析](https://natlawreview.com/article/depth-look-first-prong-dhanasar-substantial-merit-and-national-importance)
- [NatLawReview：第二项标准深入分析](https://natlawreview.com/article/depth-look-second-prong-dhanasar-well-positioned-advance-endeavor)
- [NatLawReview：第三项标准深入分析](https://natlawreview.com/article/depth-look-third-prong-dhanasar-beneficial-united-states)
- [Cyrus Mehta 博客：Matter of Dhanasar 新 NIW 标准](https://blog.cyrusmehta.com/?p=1466)

**说明：** 我没有找到 USCIS 官方政策手册的原文，以上内容主要来自律所和专业网站的二手解读。具体的子标准细节（如第一、二项的证据要求）以 uscis.gov 上的最新政策手册为准。我也没有核实近期政策变更的说法，因此没有写入上文。

The main explanation is **branch prediction**. In the loop, the `if (data[c] >= 128)` check is false for a long run of values and then true for a long run in sorted data, so the CPU predicts it well. In unsorted data the predictions often fail, which causes pipeline stalls. Some answers also note that the compiler can sometimes use a conditional move instead of a branch, which removes the penalty.

Sources:
- [Mirror of the question (backiee.wasmer.app)](https://backiee.wasmer.app/https_stackoverflow_com/questions/11227809/why-is-processing-a-sorted-array-faster)

Dense sourdough usually comes from fermentation or gluten problems, and the most common one is underproofing.

**Main causes**
- **Underproofing:** The dough hasn't fermented enough to build gas. Homegrown Happiness names under-fermentation or a weak starter as the main culprit. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
- **Overproofing:** Over-fermented dough loses gluten strength and gas escapes. Homemade Food Junkie notes this, but I couldn't open that page (it returned a 403), so I'm relying on the search summary. [Source](https://www.homemadefoodjunkie.com/?p=92373)
- **Poor gluten development:** Too few stretch-and-folds, or dough handled poorly, leaves a weak structure. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
- **Weak shaping or too little steam:** Loose shaping and a dry oven both hurt oven spring. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)

**Fixes**
- **Judge bulk fermentation by sight, not the clock.** Aim for roughly 40–50% growth, bubbles along the sides, and an airy feel. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
- **Strengthen your starter.** Feed it consistently, and use filtered water if your tap water has chlorine. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
- **Build gluten with stretch-and-folds or coil folds.** [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
- **Shape with tension** so the loaf rises up rather than out. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
- **Bake in a preheated covered pot** to trap steam. [Source](https://homegrownhappiness.com/sourdough-bread-trouble-shooting-guide/)
